subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should this issue be resolved through a refreshed/replaced Docker init timeout and fail-soft PR now, or should maintainers first require a narrower live OrbStack substep diagnosis?
rationale: Current source proves a no-deadline Docker control-plane path, but the report's exact intermittent workspace-sandbox substep is not isolated and the existing PR changes compatibility-sensitive timeout/default behavior.

options.title: Refresh or replace the timeout PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91015 as source work, but require current-main refresh, full Docker prep coverage, docs/config handling, and real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

options.title: Request live substep diagnosis first
options.body: Keep the issue open for reporter or maintainer artifacts that identify whether prune, workspace layout, Docker user resolution, or backend init is the actual slow point.

options.title: Narrow under the wedged-Docker issue
options.body: Treat the remaining actionable core work as the narrower no-timeout problem in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90980 and preserve this issue only as linked production context.

recommendation.title: Refresh or replace the timeout PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91015 as source work, but require current-main refresh, full Docker prep coverage, docs/config handling, and real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about sandbox architecture, fail-soft behavior, and config/default compatibility where path history shows repeated adjacent ownership.
